arxiv-2202-06906.title: Exel-Pardo algebras of self-similar k k -graphs
arxiv-2202-06906.creator: Hossein Larki
arxiv-2202-06906.description: Abstract . We introduce the Exel-Pardo ∗ * -algebra EP R ​ ( G , Λ ) \mathrm{EP}_{R}(G,\Lambda) associated to a self-similar k k -graph ( G , Λ , φ ) (G,\Lambda,\varphi) . We also prove the ℤ k \mathbb{Z}^{k} -graded and Cuntz-Krieger uniqueness theorems for such algebras and investigate their ideal structure.

arxiv-2308-06044.title: Going Deep and Going Wide: Counting Logic and Homomorphism Indistinguishability over Graphs of Bounded Treedepth and Treewidth
arxiv-2308-06044.creator: Eva Fluck, Tim Seppelt, Gian Luca Spitzer
arxiv-2308-06044.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Eva Fluck, Tim Seppelt, Gian Luca Spitzer. We study the expressive power of first-order logic with counting quantifiers, especially the k k -variable and quantifier-rank- q q fragment 𝖢 q k \mathsf{C}^{k}_{q} , using homomorphism indistinguishability. Recently, Dawar, Jakl, and Reggio (2021) proved that two graphs satisfy the same 𝖢 q k \mathsf{C}^{k}_{q} -sentences if and only if they are homomorphism indistinguishable over the class 𝒯 q k \mathcal{T}^{k}_{q} of graphs admitting a k k -pebble forest cover of depth q q .

arxiv-2309-10341.title: Theory of Nonequilibrium Coexistence with Coupled Conserved and Nonconserved Order Parameters
arxiv-2309-10341.creator: Daniel Evans, Ahmad K. Omar
arxiv-2309-10341.description: Abstract Phase separation routinely occurs in both living and synthetic systems. These phases are often complex and distinguished by features including crystallinity, nematic order, and a host of other nonconserved order parameters. For systems at equilibrium, the phase boundaries that characterize these transitions can be straightforwardly determined through the framework of thermodynamics.

arxiv-2310-16877.title: Primordial Black Holes with QCD Color Charge
arxiv-2310-16877.creator: Elba Alonso-Monsalve, David I. Kaiser
arxiv-2310-16877.description: Abstract We describe a realistic mechanism whereby black holes with significant QCD color charge could have formed during the early universe. Primordial black holes (PBHs) could make up a significant fraction of the dark matter if they formed well before the QCD confinement transition.

arxiv-2310-20069.title: Strong completeness of a first-order temporal logic for real time
arxiv-2310-20069.creator: Robert Goldblatt
arxiv-2310-20069.description: Abstract Propositional temporal logic over the real number time flow is finitely axiomatisable, but its first-order counterpart is not recursively axiomatisable. We study the logic that combines the propositional axiomatisation with the usual axioms for first-order logic with identity, and develop an alternative “admissible” semantics for it, showing that it is strongly complete for admissible models over the reals.

We present a sharp condition on P P guaranteeing the existence of asymptotically larger bounds in Bombieri’s inequality, so for every homogeneous polynomial q m q_{m} of degree m m we have ‖ P ​ q m ‖ a ≥ C P ​ m l ⁡ ( P ) / 2 ​ ‖ q m ‖ a , \left\|Pq_{m}\right\|_{a}\geq C_{P}m^{l\left(P\right)/2}\left\|q_{m}\right\|_{a}, where ∥ ⋅ ∥ a \|\cdot\|_{a} denotes the apolar norm.

arxiv-2412-13866.title: SHAP scores fail pervasively even when Lipschitz succeeds
arxiv-2412-13866.creator: Olivier Létoffé, Xuanxiang Huang, Joao Marques-Silva
arxiv-2412-13866.description: Abstract The ubiquitous use of Shapley values in eXplainable AI (XAI) has been triggered by the tool SHAP, and as a result are commonly referred to as SHAP scores. Recent work devised examples of machine learning (ML) classifiers for which the computed SHAP scores are thoroughly unsatisfactory, by allowing human decision-makers to be misled.

arxiv-2504-07254.title: Reinforcement Learning Dynamics of Network Vaccination and Hysteresis: A Double-Edged Sword for Addressing Vaccine Hesitancy
arxiv-2504-07254.creator: Atticus McWhorter, Feng Fu
arxiv-2504-07254.description: Abstract Mass vaccination remains a long-lasting challenge for disease control and prevention with upticks in vaccine hesitancy worldwide. Here, we introduce an experience-based learning (Q-learning) dynamics model of vaccination behavior in social networks, where agents choose whether or not to vaccinate given environmental feedbacks from their local neighborhood.

arxiv-2509-23666.title: Beyond Greedy Exits: Improved Early Exit Decisions for Risk Control and Reliability
arxiv-2509-23666.creator: Divya Jyoti Bajpai & Manjesh Kumar Hanawal
arxiv-2509-23666.description: Abstract Early-Exit Deep Neural Networks enable adaptive inference by allowing prediction at intermediary layers, significantly reducing computational costs and latency. Most of the early exit strategies greedily exit a sample at an intermediary layer if the confidence in class prediction exceeds a predefined threshold that is set using a static validation set.

arxiv-2512-06414.title: A Factorization of the Log-Concavity Operator for Pascal Determinantal Arrays and Their Infinite Row-Wise Log-Concavity
arxiv-2512-06414.creator: Hossein Teimoori, Hasan Khodakarami
arxiv-2512-06414.description: Abstract We study the Pascal determinantal arrays PD k \operatorname{PD}_{k} , whose entries PD k ⁡ ( i , j ) \operatorname{PD}_{k}(i,j) are the k × k k\times k minors of the lower-triangular Pascal matrix P = ( ( a b ) ) a , b ≥ 0 P=(\binom{a}{b})_{a,b\geq 0} .

pmc-10574070.title: Herbal Remedies for Constipation-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
pmc-10574070.creator: Giuseppe Chiarioni, Stefan Lucian Popa, Abdulrahman Ismaiel, Cristina Pop, Dinu Iuliu Dumitrascu, Vlad Dumitru Brata, Traian Adrian Duse, Victor Incze, Teodora Surdea-Blaga, Jose Antonio Uranga
pmc-10574070.description: Background: Constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C) is a common gastrointestinal disorder characterized by abdominal pain and altered bowel habits. Conventional treatments for IBS-C often provide limited efficiency, leading to an increasing interest in exploring herbal remedies. This systematic review aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of herbal remedies in the management of IBS-C.

pmc-11438393.title: Assessing quality and reliability of online videos on tachycardia: a YouTube video-based study
pmc-11438393.creator: Zexi Li, Chunyi Yan, Xiaojun Lyu, Fanghui Li, Rui Zeng
pmc-11438393.description: BackgroundConsidering the adverse clinical consequences of pathologic tachycardia and the potential anxiety caused by physiological tachycardia in some heathy individuals, it is imperative to disseminate health information related to tachycardia for promotion in early diagnosis and appropriate management. YouTube has been increasingly used to access health care information.

pmc-11547925.title: DNA Methylation Signatures Characterize Gene Expression Modulation in Lung Cancer Patients Affected by Anorexia
pmc-11547925.creator: Alessio Molfino, Francesca Ambrosani, Silvia Udali, Giovanni Imbimbo, Sara Moruzzi, Annalisa Castagna, Patrizia Pattini, Federica Tambaro, Cesarina Ramaccini, Maurizio Muscaritoli, Simonetta Friso
pmc-11547925.description: Background/Objectives: The pathophysiology of cancer anorexia is multifactorial and unclear. Transcriptomic analysis from PBMCs RNA showed diverse patterns of gene expression pathways in anorexic cancer patients. We assessed whether the different transcriptomic signatures are modulated by DNA methylation in lung cancer patients presenting with poor appetite.

pmc-11676076.title: Concomitant Potentially Contagious Factors Detected in Poland and Regarding Acanthamoeba Strains, Etiological Agents of Keratitis in Humans
pmc-11676076.creator: Lidia Chomicz, Jacek P Szaflik, Agnieszka Kuligowska, David Bruce Conn, Wanda Baltaza, Beata Szostakowska, Paweł J Zawadzki, Monika Dybicz, Anna Machalińska, Konrad Perkowski, Anna Bajer, Jerzy Szaflik, Juan Carlos Gutiérrez, Antonella d’Arminio Monforte
pmc-11676076.description: Background: Diseases in humans caused by amphizoic amoebae that can result in visual impairment and even blindness, have recently been identified more frequently worldwide. Etiologically complex incidents of keratitis, including those connected with Acanthamoeba strains detected in Poland, were evaluated in this study.

pmc-12374706.title: Efficacy and Safety of the Multi-Level Comprehensive Collateral Artery Embolism Sequential Hepatic Arterial Infusion Chemotherapy, Combined with TKI and ICI, for Unresectable Huge Hepatocellular Carcinoma (>10cm): A Propensity Score Matching Cohort Study
pmc-12374706.creator: Hao-yang Tan, Shuang-quan Liu, Yan-han Liu, Jiu-ling Zheng, Hua-guo Feng
pmc-12374706.description: ObjectiveThis retrospective study was conducted to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of a new combination therapy of the multi-level comprehensive collateral artery embolism (CAE) sequential hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC), tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) for unresectable huge hepatocellular carcinoma (>10cm) patients.MethodsA propensity score-matching (PSM) cohort study was conducted.

pmc-13049364.title: Glia Are Bussin’: How Single‐Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Enlighten the Role of Neuroglia in Spinal Cord Injury and Regeneration
pmc-13049364.creator: Julio Mejia, Philip J. Horner
pmc-13049364.description: The impact that single‐cell and spatial genomic technologies have had on the scientific community since their advent has been widespread and profound. The field of spinal cord injury (SCI) is one such area that has experienced an increased implementation of genomic technologies within recent years.

pmc-13169736.title: Attitude and subjective norms as predictors of intention of married men and women to accept caesarean section delivery in Lagos, Nigeria
pmc-13169736.creator: Titilayo Abike Olaoye, Boluwatife Adebambo, Blessing Osie-Efetie, Ololade Ogunsanmi, Clarita Panuel-Egwakhe, Saratu Ajike, Juliana Olwatoyin Elebiju, Favour Ayobola Ojo, Nnodimele Onuigbo Atulomah
pmc-13169736.description: BackgroundDespite its life-saving benefits, there is reluctance among Nigerian women and their husbands to have a caesarean section (CS) when indicated. This study assessed attitude and associated subjective norms involved in resolving whether to accept CS delivery among married men and women in Lagos, Nigeria.MethodsThis was a cross-sectional survey.

pmc-13300528.title: Transitioning from Laboratory-Developed Tests to a Single Commercial Reagent Kit in a National Newborn Screening Program: Impact on Analytical Performance and Harmonization
pmc-13300528.creator: Rachel S. Carling, Zoe J. Barclay, Sophie C. Ward, Marie Appleton, Robert Barski, Harry Benn, Kelly Chambers, Paul Coakley, Helena Kemp, Nicola Crabbe, Sarah Dowden, Toby Greenfield, Sarah L. Hogg, Saima Hussein, Rhiannon Marr, Oliver Parkes, Darren Powell, Tejswurree Ramgoolam, Joshua Ssali, Nazia
pmc-13300528.description: Newborn screening in England is a national program with laboratories adhering to common screening algorithms. Until recently, screening for inherited metabolic disorders was provided by ten laboratories using laboratory-developed tests (LDTs) and three using commercial assays: harmonization of results proved challenging.

pmc-13352655.title: Diagnostic accuracy of AI-assisted point-of-care ultrasound for abdominal free fluid detection in FAST trauma assessment: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13352655.creator: Ali Çelik, Ensar Topaloğlu, Mümin Murat Yazıcı
pmc-13352655.description: Study objectivePoint-of-care ultrasound (PoCUS) is widely used in trauma care through the Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (FAST) protocol, but its accuracy is highly operator-dependent. Artificial intelligence (AI) may reduce variability and improve reliability. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of AI-assisted PoCUS for detecting free fluid in trauma patients.

pmc-13612887.title: The Relationship Between Age, Brain Structure, and Cognition in Chronic Traumatic Brain Injury
pmc-13612887.creator: Amber Ayton, Jennie Ponsford, Amelia J Hicks, Rachael Knott, Gavin Gan, Gershon Spitz
pmc-13612887.description: BackgroundThe long-term impact of traumatic brain injury (TBI) on ageing remains poorly understood without controlled studies.ObjectiveCross-sectionally examine how chronic moderate–severe TBI and advancing age interact to affect brain structure and related cognition in adults aged 40 to 90 years who received compensated inpatient rehabilitation in Australia.
